correctness.rationale: Independence and exact geometric sums give P(W=0)=c and P(W=k)=c(q^k+r^k). The PGF has a log expansion with positive odd and square-form even jump intensities, summable because q,r<1, so defines a compound-Poisson law. Bouzar Proposition 1 proves the applicable canonical monotonicity criterion; after sorting q>=r, the only nontrivial inequalities are (1-t^m)^2>=q(1+t^(2m+1)), whose left side increases and right side decreases, reducing all m>=1 to m=1. LC discriminants are explicit and the k=1 boundary is checked. The checker is supplementary.

value.rationale: The folded magnitude of a skew signed count difference is a natural observable. Since absolute value does not preserve signed compound-Poisson decompositions, positivity of its exact folded jump measure is nontrivial. The sharp two-dimensional phase boundary for binomial-thinning self-decomposability answers a natural structural question in full and contrasts with the separate symmetric LC regime; it is neither an arbitrary slice nor a small numeric improvement.
